state.goal: Assess a minimal complete CanLang toolchain for its first managed Cloudflare deployment. Adoption is the primary objective; compact AI-authored sources and one canonical route per SaaS primitive serve it. Reuse established facilities: the user explicitly rejects rebuilding generic UTF-8 support. This is research and advice only; no compiler, runtime, infrastructure or standard library implementation is authorized in this round.
state.status: The repository has 44 .can sources, a Python syntax parser and 20 hand-written JavaScript desired-output targets including CanCRM, with UI revisions being completed. They do not implement a semantic compiler, operation runtime or shared imports. Apps must compile directly from .can to JavaScript ES modules for workerd. A possible future standard library is authored in TypeScript and type-checked/emitted as JavaScript in its own release build, not through a per-app TypeScript stage. Compiler implementation language is not selected here. Existing parser work should not be discarded merely to unify tooling.
state.platform: Workers exposes TextEncoder/TextDecoder and their streams for UTF-8, Request/Response/fetch, streams, Web Crypto, native Intl and JavaScript built-ins. D1/R2/DO/Queues/email are provisioned Cloudflare bindings, not automatically supplied by standalone workerd. Node compatibility is partial; some Wrangler-injected imports have nonfunctional methods. Current docs enable Node compatibility by default at compatibility_date >= 2026-08-04; earlier dates have their own flag requirements. Pin the date/tool releases and verify APIs actually used. Sources: https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/web-standards/ ; https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/nodejs/ ; https://github.com/cloudflare/workerd
state.packaging: Wrangler already bundles with esbuild, honors workerd conditional exports, provides dev/deploy and a dry-run bundle, and accepts generated configuration. Its bundled esbuild version can change with Wrangler releases. --no-bundle disables its processing, including polyfill injection. Owning an explicit esbuild step permits more direct build settings/artifact control but needs equivalent module/polyfill integration. Direct Cloudflare API upload can provide control and avoid the Wrangler dependency, but module/assets packaging, auth/configuration, provisioning/update behavior and development/test integration must then be supplied by CanLang or other tools. None is a demonstrated performance winner. Sources: https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/wrangler/bundling/ ; https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/wrangler/configuration/#generated-wrangler-configuration
state.examples: Inline BDD fixtures and tables must execute the generated canonical operation, keep each example row isolated, preserve authored expected values, check no committed effects on rejection and never contact live providers. Cloudflare currently supplies @cloudflare/vitest-plugin; it runs Vitest tests in workerd using Miniflare/bindings with per-file storage isolation and testing APIs for scheduled events, queues, DO alarms and migrations. Per-file isolation is not itself per-row isolation: generated fixture/reset behavior must supply that. A custom direct-workerd runner can avoid Vitest/plugin conventions and focus on CanLang examples, but must own orchestration, binding configuration, isolation, effect inspection and reporting. Neither path proves remote provider behavior, distributed correctness or production performance. Use one canonical automated path rather than stack custom simulators and multiple suites. Sources: https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/testing/vitest-integration/ ; https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/testing/vitest-integration/isolation-and-concurrency/ ; https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/testing/vitest-integration/test-apis/
state.boundaries: Selected app/import closure, types and effects, CRUD schemas/defaults, policy-first reads, final-state invariants and dependency rechecks, pre-state locks, bounded work, exact numeric/wire/storage adapters, operation identity/replay, atomic commit semantics, interface/UI generation and explicit migration rules remain CanLang responsibilities. Generic MCP/ICU/decimal/auth libraries are reuse candidates only when their contracts match; native APIs and third-party libraries do not prove these semantics. Generated Worker configuration, SQL/assets/tests and version-pinned library dependency metadata are tooling artifacts; apps must not author wrapper apps, repeated source/dependency lists or a second build manifest. Account credentials, binding IDs and deployment mappings cannot be invented from app names.

packaging.instructions: Which initial packaging/deployment route best fits the supplied scope, reuse constraint and maintenance goals? Weigh concrete control and integration benefits against dependencies and implementation work; do not infer measured speed or correctness from tool choice.

criteria.wrangler_bundle: Have CanLang emit app JS and derived artifacts/configuration, then let pinned Wrangler perform its normal bundling and deployment. Reuse platform integration and local development while accepting its dependency and bundled-esbuild behavior.
criteria.explicit_esbuild: Have CanLang own a pinned esbuild packaging step and use Wrangler --no-bundle to deploy its prepared artifacts. Gain direct packaging control while taking responsibility for missing bundling integration, including required polyfills/module handling.
criteria.api_upload: Build and upload through the Cloudflare API without Wrangler as the main deployment tool. Gain direct control of deployment requests and dependency policy while supplying equivalent packaging, platform configuration, auth and development/test integration.
criteria.unresolved: Leave the initial packaging route undecided until further constraints or a concrete unsupported capability distinguish these viable routes.

examples.instructions: Which single automated execution path should initially host the inline CanLang examples? Compare existing workerd integration with a dedicated runner, accounting for row isolation, real operation execution and reporting without claiming distributed coverage.

criteria.official_vitest: Generate the inline examples for Vitest with @cloudflare/vitest-plugin and CanLang fixture/effect assertions. Reuse maintained workerd/binding integration while accepting the tool dependency and supplying per-row isolation beyond the plugin's per-file isolation.
criteria.custom_workerd: Generate examples for a dedicated runner driving workerd directly. Control execution/reporting around CanLang alone while implementing process/binding setup, per-row isolation, effect observation and recovery instead of using the official integration.
criteria.unresolved: Defer the execution-host selection because the known tool contracts and example requirements do not establish a suitable initial canonical path.
